transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-21
Time: 15:00 PT / 18:00 ET
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ariel Russo (Redwood AE), Diego Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Wu (Tungsten Head of Partnerships), Omar Haddad (Tungsten Cloud Infra Lead), Priya Singh (Tungsten Solutions Architect)

Summary:
Quick partner intro between Redwood and Tungsten Cloud to align on potential channel/reseller relationship for Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments. Main focus: applicability of Tungsten's accelerator hardware for Redwood's inference runtime, networking/VPC integration patterns, compliance gaps, and a pilot scope (benchmarks + reseller commercial model).

Topics:
- Accelerator hardware and instance types
- Dedicated vs hosted routing and pricing levers
- VPC/private deployment integration and KMS
- Pilot scope: perf targets, datasets, and timelines
- Legal/commercial handoff for reseller conversation

Action items (captured verbally in call): see metadata section above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ariel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ariel Russo from Redwood, AE on the channel motion. Diego and I will cover technical fit and next steps. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Lena: Hi Ariel, doing well. Excited to learn more, thanks for setting this up.
[00:17] Omar: Hey all, Omar here. Quick note, we'll be evaluating the hardware and network requirements — trying to assess whether this is an onramp we can sell to our enterprise accounts.
[00:28] Diego: Great — Diego Patel, SE. I'm going to ask a few questions about your accelerator variants and typical workload shapes so we can map to Redwood's batching/K V cache strategies.
[00:40] Priya: Awesome. We're mostly serving two workloads: short text generation for customer support (avg seq 128) and longer summarization (avg seq 1024) for analytics. P95 latency targets vary by tenant but generally 120-250ms for the short path.
[00:59] Ariel: That's helpful. Two immediate flags — sequence length will drive kernel selection and effective batching. Also curious if your accelerators expose large per-card memory for KV cache because that impacts mid-context performance.
[01:18] Omar: Yes, our T-RT cards (v3) have 48GB HBM and a software SDK for shared KV caching. There's some nuance around multi-tenant isolation though.
[01:32] Diego: Perfect, that helps. On Redwood's side our runtime picks kernels by model arch and sequence distribution; we also do continuous batching and prefix caching. For 128 tokens it's usually safe to prioritize latency SLO with smaller batch windows. For 1k sequences we lean into quantized model variants and larger batching.
[01:55] Lena: Can you expand on quantized model variants? Our sales folks raised questions about quality delta.
[02:03] Diego: Sure — we typically test int8 and 4-bit QAT/ PTQ variants depending on model. For many transformer families the delta is minor for prompts we care about, but we validate with eval sets. We'll produce quality vs cost curves during the pilot.
[02:20] Priya: Will that require us to host models or does Redwood manage that?
[02:27] Ariel: Options. Hosted API for fast go-to-market, Dedicated (reserved pools) where Redwood manages runtime in your region, or Private (VPC/on-prem) where the control plane is customer-managed and you host model artifacts. For Tungsten reseller model we'd likely start with Dedicated or Private depending on security needs.
[02:46] Omar: Important point: many of our customers require VPC-only endpoints and customer-managed KMS/HSM. How does Redwood handle KMS integration?
[02:55] Diego: We support KMS integrations and can work with cloud KMS or HSM via the private control plane. There may be a small ops piece to wire the keys and certs. We also generate audit logs for inference requests.
[03:10] Lena: And SOC2/ISO? A lot of legal questions come up.
[03:15] Ariel: Redwood has SOC2 Type II. We also have compliance summary docs and can run through a questionnaire. I'll share the SOC2 summary and the private deployment checklist after the call.
[03:26] Priya: Great. From infra perspective, how do you route requests between hosted and dedicated? Is there smart routing by policy?
[03:34] Diego: Yes — our smart router can route by latency, cost, region, or customer tier. If a model variant isn't available on a particular pool we fall back to a compatible variant. You can configure policies to prefer low latency or low cost.
[03:47] Omar: Ok. On throughput: our reseller customers often need burst capacity above reserved numbers, like spikes 3-5x for marketing events. Do you support burst or autoscale?
[03:59] Ariel: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity. We can set burst buffer and also a fallback to hosted if reserved pools are exhausted, but fallback may change cost and latency profiles.
[04:12] Priya: Does fallback mean data goes over the public Redwood API? Can we restrict that?
[04:19] Diego: You can configure strict private-only routing, but then you'd need to commit enough capacity or accept queueing. Alternatively, we can set policy to fallback only to specific verified regions or partner pools — that's something we'll architect with Tungsten.
[04:35] Lena: How about model versions and deploys? We need safe rollouts for customers.
[04:41] Ariel: We do canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. Also per-route/model dashboards and tracing for debugging regressions.
[04:54] Omar: For the pilot, we will need a performance baseline and then test with your quantized profiles. What's a realistic timeline?
[05:02] Diego: If you can share a representative workload and dataset, we can run an SE benchmark within a week of receiving it. Setup for a Private pilot may take longer because of KMS and VPC peering — typically 2-4 weeks.
[05:18] Priya: For datasets, we cannot share PII. We can sanitize or provide synthetic workloads.
[05:24] Diego: That's fine — synthetic is common. We can also support in-situ tests if you prefer.
[05:31] Lena: On the commercial side, what's the reseller split / referral model?
[05:36] Ariel: We have a few options: referral fee, channel reseller where Tungsten sells Redwood Dedicated capacity with a margin, or co-sell discounts for pilots. I'd like to loop in our partnerships lead after this so legal/commercial can talk specifics.
[05:52] Omar: Who are common competitors you're seeing in this space?
[05:56] Ariel: Companies like NimbusGrid and Aurora Compute get mentioned — mostly around self-hosted runtimes. We differentiate with unified API across hosted/dedicated/private and the developer experience.
[06:07] Priya: Network egress is a big concern for our customers. If Redwood routes to hosted fallback, that could incur additional egress fees.
[06:15] Diego: Good point — we'll include estimated egress exposure in the cost model we share. For Dedicated within your cloud region, egress is minimal.
[06:27] Lena: Ok, can we talk hardware specifics — are there driver/SDK requirements for the T-RT cards?
[06:33] Omar: We expose a runtime SDK that can mount into containerized stacks. There is a shim for NV-like drivers; we can provide docs.
[06:41] Diego: From Redwood's perspective we generally run models in containerized runtime with specific kernel and CUDA-like optimizations. If your SDK is container friendly, integration is straightforward. We may need to tune few kernels for the T-RT instruction set.
[06:58] Priya: Anything we should be aware of for quantization compatibility? Some hardware prefers specific layouts.
[07:04] Diego: Yes — quantization layout and fast-path kernels differ. We'll do a short compatibility scan during the pilot and produce recommended quantization profiles.
[07:15] Lena: For the channel, it's important that we have a simple onboarding flow for our systems integrators. If we resell Dedicated, do you offer a partner console or API for provisioning?
[07:26] Ariel: We have partner APIs for provisioning dedicated pools and quotas. We also provide templates and automation scripts. For reseller scenarios, we can grant partner scopes or managed accounts.
[07:38] Omar: Security: SSO/SAML and RBAC? We need fine-grained roles for tenant admins.
[07:45] Diego: We support SSO with SAML/OIDC, and RBAC for route-level permissions. Audit logs are retained per customer and can be shipped to your SIEM.
[07:56] Priya: On the pilot dataset — we want to validate latency and hallucination rates. Can Redwood run evals that check output quality regressions?
[08:04] Diego: Yes — we tie quality monitoring to eval suites and set regression alerts. We'll need a set of prompts and expected outputs or a scoring rubric.
[08:15] Lena: Great. Let's outline a minimal pilot scope now so we can align calendar.
[08:20] Ariel: Proposal: 2-week bench where Redwood runs hosted/dedicated/private variants on Tungsten T-RT instances using synthetic workloads for short and long sequences. Deliverables: perf report (latency/throughput/cost), quality curves for quantized variants, and an integration checklist.
[08:37] Omar: 2-week bench sounds good, but Private setup could push us to 3–4 weeks. We can accept that as long as milestones are clear.
[08:46] Priya: Agree. Also want a list of required IAM roles and network ports so infra can review.
[08:52] Diego: We'll produce an infra checklist including VPC/subnet CIDRs, peering, KMS roles, and firewall rules.
[08:59] Ariel: Next steps I propose: I'll share the deck and SOC2/compliance summary; Diego will scope estimation and schedule the SE benchmark; Lena will coordinate legal and reseller framework. Any objections?
[09:10] Lena: No objections. We'll gather the sample workload and target SLOs.
[09:15] Omar: We'll also check the T-RT SDK docs and send a link.
[09:19] Priya: One more question — latency SLO for short path, you said 120-250ms p95. Can you propose where Redwood typically lands on p95 for 128 token workloads on dedicated quantized setups?
[09:30] Diego: Ballpark: on optimized GPUs with low batch windows we often hit 50-90ms p95 for 128 tokens on int8; on partner accelerators it depends on kernel maturity — initial runs may be 80-200ms until we tune kernels. We'll refine during the bench.
[09:50] Ariel: I'll capture that as an expectation open item.
[09:54] Lena: Ok that's helpful. Anything else we should flag before wrapping?
[10:00] Omar: Licensing — do you require model artifact hosting on Redwood for Dedicated?
[10:06] Ariel: For Dedicated we can host the runtime; model artifacts can either be hosted by Redwood or customer-managed in Private. Licensing depends on model vendor — open models are straightforward; third-party licensed models will need separate agreements.
[10:21] Priya: We'll catalog which models our top customers use and share it.
[10:25] Diego: Perfect.
[10:28] Ariel: Alright — let's recap quickly and then we'll close.
[10:32] Diego: Recap: Redwood to run bench on Tungsten T-RT; we'll test int8 and 4-bit quant; provide perf and quality reports; share infra checklist and compliance docs; schedule SE benchmark next week.
[10:46] Lena: Sounds good. We'll get the workloads and connect legal.
[10:49] Omar: Thanks everyone.
[10:51] Ariel: Thanks — we'll follow up with the deck and scheduler.
[10:55] Priya: Thanks, bye.

Note: Transcript contains some automated transcription artifacts; acronyms like K V cache, V P C, and SAML may be spaced or mis-cased in places.
